data.name: NoCommand
data.value: Give a command: apply or undo.

data.name: ReplaceNeedsValues
data.value: --replace needs two values: the text to find and the new text.

data.name: CaseNeedsValue
data.value: --case needs a value: lower, upper, title or sentence.

data.name: BadCase
data.value: "{0}" is not a value of --case: use lower, upper, title or sentence.

data.name: EmptyFind
data.value: The text to find in --replace cannot be empty.

data.name: TwoFolders
data.value: Give one folder only: "{0}" and "{1}" were both given.

data.name: NoFolder
data.value: Give the folder to rename in.

data.name: NoRule
data.value: Give at least one rule option, such as --replace or --case.

data.name: EmptyPrefix
data.value: The text of --prefix cannot be empty.

data.name: EmptySuffix
data.value: The text of --suffix cannot be empty.

data.name: EmptyInsert
data.value: The text of --insert cannot be empty.

data.name: InsertNeedsValues
data.value: --insert needs two values: the text and the position.

data.name: BadInsertPosition
data.value: "{0}" is not a position of --insert: use a whole number from 1.

data.name: BadChoice
data.value: "{0}" is not a value of {1}: use {2}.

data.name: PresetExists
data.value: A preset named "{0}" exists. Add --overwrite to replace it.

data.name: PresetSaveFailed
data.value: The preset could not be saved: {0}

data.name: PresetNameTooLong
data.value: A preset name has at most 100 characters.

data.name: BlankText
data.value: The text of {0} cannot be empty or only spaces.

data.name: BlankExtension
data.value: The text of {0} cannot be empty or only dots and spaces.

data.name: EmptyOptionText
data.value: The text of {0} cannot be empty.

data.name: RegexNeedsValues
data.value: --regex needs two values: the pattern and the replacement.

data.name: QuoteInFolder
data.value: The folder {0} contains a quote: remove the backslash before the closing quote, as in "D:\Pics" instead of "D:\Pics\".

data.name: InvalidFolder
data.value: "{0}" is not a valid folder path.

data.name: FolderIsFile
data.value: {0} is a file, not a folder.

data.name: UnexpectedBeforeRename
data.value: NameShift hit an unexpected problem. No file was renamed.

data.name: UnexpectedBeforeUndo
data.value: NameShift hit an unexpected problem. No file was changed.

data.name: UndoHistoryUnusable
data.value: The undo history cannot be used: a rename was cut short or the history file is unreadable. No file was changed.

data.name: UndoOnlyDryRun
data.value: undo takes no folder or rule options, only --dry-run.

data.name: HelpMain
data.value:
NameShiftCmd renames the files of a folder in one step, and lists the new names first with --dry-run.
Other usage: NameShiftCmd help NameShiftCmd --version
Commands: apply Rename the files of a folder with rule options. undo Take back the last batch (also one made in the window). help Show this help.
Options: --help, -h, /? Show this help (the same as the help command). --version Show the version of NameShiftCmd.
Examples: NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --replace IMG Trip --dry-run NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --case lower NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --preset Photos --dry-run NameShiftCmd undo --dry-run NameShiftCmd apply --help

data.name: HelpApply
data.value:
Options of apply: --replace <find> <with> Replace <find> with <with> in each file name. --case <mode> Change the case: lower, upper, title or sentence. --prefix <text> Add <text> before each name. --suffix <text> Add <text> after each name, before the extension. --insert <text> <pos> Insert <text> at character <pos> (from 1). --from-end Count the --insert position from the end. --word-space Put a space between joined words (camelCase). --number Number the files: suffix, from 1, step 1. --number-mode prefix|suffix|insert Where the number goes. --number-start <n> The first number, written in the chosen system. --number-step <n> Add <n> to the number for each next file. --number-pad <n> The minimum number of digits (decimal, hex). --number-separator <text> The text between the name and the number. --number-position <n> The character the number goes at (insert mode). --number-system decimal|hex|letters|roman The kind of numbers written. --number-case upper|lower Capital or small letters (not for decimal). --name-fixed <text> Replace the name (not the extension) with <text>. --name-empty Make the name empty (not the extension). --name-reverse Reverse the letters of the name. --ext-lower Write the extension in small letters. --ext-upper Write the extension in capital letters. --ext-fixed <text> Replace the extension with <text>. --ext-extra <text> Add <text> as a second extension (a.txt.bak). --ext-remove Remove the extension. --remove-first <n> Remove the first <n> characters. --remove-last <n> Remove the last <n> characters. --remove-from <n> Remove from character <n>; needs --remove-to. --remove-to <n> Remove up to character <n>; needs --remove-from. --remove-chars <text> Remove every one of the characters in <text>. --remove-text <text> Remove the text <text> wherever it is found. --remove-before <text> Remove everything before the first <text>. --remove-after <text> Remove everything after the first <text>. --remove-whole-word With --remove-text: only whole words. --remove-match-case Make the text options care about capitals. --remove-keep-marker Keep the marker text of before or after. --remove-digits Remove the digits. --remove-symbols Remove the symbols. --remove-accents Remove the accents from letters. --remove-high-chars Remove the characters that are not plain ASCII. --remove-trim Remove spaces at the start and the end. --remove-leading-dots Remove dots at the start. --remove-double-spaces Turn runs of spaces into one space. --regex <pattern> <replacement> Replace regex matches; $1 and ${name} work. --regex-ignore-case With --regex: ignore capitals when matching. --regex-extension With --regex: also change the extension. --move <n> Move <n> characters of the name elsewhere. --copy <n> Copy <n> characters of the name elsewhere. --move-from start|end With --move or --copy: take from the start or end. --move-to start|end|position With --move or --copy: where they go. --move-position <n> With --move or --copy: the character for position. --move-separator <text> With --move or --copy: text between the parts. --date Add the file date: modified, yyyy-MM-dd, prefix. --date-source modified|created Which date of the file to use. --date-format <format> The date as a .NET format, such as yyyyMMdd. --date-placement prefix|suffix Put the date before or after the name. --date-separator <text> The text between the date and the name. --folder-name Add the name of the folder (1 level, prefix). --folder-levels <n> How many folder names to add (nearest first). --folder-placement prefix|suffix Put the folder name before or after the name. --folder-separator <text> The text between the folder name and the name. --preset <name> Use the rules of a preset saved in the window. --save-preset <name> Save the rules as a preset (also with --dry-run). --overwrite Let --save-preset replace a preset of that name. --dry-run Only list the new names; rename nothing. --quiet, -q Print nothing on success; errors are still shown. --verbose, -v Also list the renamed and the unchanged files. --help, -h, /? Show this help. Give at least one rule option. Options can come in any order.
Example of apply: NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --replace IMG Trip --case lower --dry-run

data.name: HelpUndo
data.value:
Options of undo: --dry-run List the names undo would restore; change nothing. Checks the files and the history; changes nothing. --help, -h, /? Show this help. Undo takes back the last batch, also one made in the window.
Example of undo: NameShiftCmd undo --dry-run

data.name: ExitCode0
data.value: Done, or nothing to rename or undo.

data.name: ExitCode1
data.value: Usage or input error (the command line or the folder). Nothing renamed.

data.name: ExitCode2
data.value: Conflicts or rule errors. Nothing renamed.

data.name: ExitCode3
data.value: Nothing changed (refused, rolled back, no history, or a crash before it).

data.name: ExitCode4
data.value: Look at the disk: items left renamed or not restored, no history, a crash.
